meta.subtitle: Samsara has turned GAAP-profitable with growth near 30%, but the current-year multiple already pays for a growth rate that is slowing.

analystSentiment.commentary: Coverage is bullish. Of 25 analysts, 19 rate Samsara Buy, 6 Hold and none Sell, for a consensus Buy. The consensus price target is $52.16, 34.1% above the September 24, 2026 price, with a median of $53.00 and a range of $39.00 to $60.00. The shares trade just below even the lowest target, so every analyst in the count sees some upside. No analyst rationale was captured, so we cannot say which assumptions drive those targets. We land one notch below the consensus, at HOLD, for the reasons argued in the valuation section, where our Bull case takes the Street's median target as its anchor.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Samsara Inc. sells the Connected Operations Platform, which ingests data from its IoT devices and from connected assets and third-party systems, with embedded capabilities for AI, workflows and analytics. Its applications include video-based safety, telematics and site visibility. Customers span transportation, construction, wholesale and retail trade, field services, logistics, manufacturing, utilities and energy, government, healthcare and education, and food and beverage. The company was incorporated in 2015 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California. Its fiscal year ends on the Saturday closest to February 1, so fiscal 2026 ended on January 31, 2026, and the 10-Q covers the quarter ended August 1, 2026. Samsara reports as a single segment, with no product or geographic split available. It sells the platform on multi-year subscriptions: in each of its past two fiscal years, approximately 98% of revenue came from subscriptions to the platform, and the rest from replacement IoT devices, shipping and handling fees, and professional services.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body: Samsara has crossed into GAAP profitability while revenue still grows near 30%, and free cash flow has turned positive; the financials section carries the figures. The question is the price. The shares trade at a current-year earnings multiple that already pays for growth the company expects to keep slowing, and the trailing operating margin is barely above breakeven. Our scenarios leave a small expected return against a bear case that is a real downside. The business is executing, but the valuation leaves little room for a slip, so we rate the shares HOLD.

catalysts: Sustained GAAP profitability: further profitable quarters would confirm the turn described in the financials section.
Recurring-revenue growth: annual recurring revenue and large-customer counts are still rising (growth section).
Earnings delivery: consensus has EPS rising from FY2027 to FY2028, the path our Base case values.
Broader adoption: selling more Applications and Agents into existing accounts, and wider use beyond fleets, would deepen the platform (growth section).
Cash generation: free cash flow turned positive in FY2025 and rose in FY2026 (cash flow section).
risks: Valuation: the current-year multiple leaves little room for a slip in growth or margins (valuation section).
Slowing growth: annual revenue growth has slowed in each year shown, and the company expects further deceleration (risks section).
Thin operating profit: most trailing net income comes from below the operating line (financials section).
Dilution: equity compensation is the capital-allocation item that matters most for outside holders (management section).
Founder voting control: insiders hold most of the vote through ten-vote Class B shares (management section).

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended Saturday closest to Feb 1 (52/53-wk).

financials.incomeCommentary:
Revenue for the quarter ended August 1, 2026 was $508.4 million, {+ up 29.9% +} from $391.5 million a year earlier. That quarter is the second quarter of Samsara's fiscal 2027; the snapshot labels it "Q3'26" on a calendar mapping, so we refer to it by its end date. Net income was {+ $16.2 million +}, against a net loss of $16.8 million a year earlier, and for the six months ended August 1, 2026 net income was $60.8 million against a $38.9 million loss. The 10-K says the company had incurred net losses in each period since incorporation before the third quarter of fiscal 2026, and fiscal 2026 as a whole still closed with a net loss of $9.1 million, so the turn is recent.

The profit is thinner at the operating line. The trailing operating margin is 1.0%, the same as the latest quarter's, while the trailing net margin is 4.9%, so most trailing profit comes from below the operating line. The MD&A says that line consists primarily of income on money market funds and marketable debt securities and gains or losses on strategic investments, income that tracks the investment portfolio rather than the platform.

Over the five fiscal years shown, operating margin improved from -82.6% in FY2022 to -3.2% in FY2026, and gross margin rose from 70.9% to 76.7%. The trailing gross margin of 76.4% sits slightly below the FY2026 level, for reasons the captured filings do not give; the MD&A says cost of revenue may increase as a result of higher market prices for hardware components. Revenue growth slowed each year, from 52.3% in FY2023 to 29.6% in FY2026. The margin turn is real but early, and growth is decelerating.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended Saturday closest to Feb 1 (52/53-wk).

financials.balanceCommentary: The balance sheet shows no strain, with one caveat about what was captured. Cash and short-term investments were $0.3B at the end of FY2026, down from $0.9B in FY2022 after a low of $0.1B in FY2024, and total equity was $1.4B. The current ratio was 1.64 at fiscal year-end and is 1.62 on a trailing basis. Total debt and net debt show a dash in every year; we read a dash as not captured, so we do not describe the company as debt-free. The 10-K reports an accumulated deficit of $1,619.1 million as of January 31, 2026, the cumulative cost of the loss-making years. The MD&A adds that Samsara maintains a full valuation allowance against its U.S. deferred tax assets because it has concluded their realization is not more likely than not; we read that as a reminder that profitability is recent. Solvency is not the issue in this name; valuation and dilution are.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended Saturday closest to Feb 1 (52/53-wk).

financials.cashflowCommentary: Free cash flow turned before earnings did. FCF was $207.4M in FY2026, a 12.8% margin, after an 8.9% margin in FY2025 and negative margins from FY2022 through FY2024 (-44.6%, -20.9% and -2.4%). FY2026 capital expenditure was $28.8M, small against operating cash flow, so most operating cash reaches free cash flow. FY2026 free cash flow sat well above the full-year net loss noted in the income discussion; no breakdown of that gap was captured, and the equity compensation discussed under capital allocation may account for part of it. The dividend yield is 0.00%, and the share-repurchase line shows a dash for FY2025 and FY2026, which we read, like the debt line, as not captured. Cash generation is real and rising, but at the trailing FCF yield discussed under valuation, cash flow alone does not support the price.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: The trailing multiples carry little information. The P/E is 243.1x and EV/EBITDA is 722.2x because trailing earnings and EBITDA sit close to zero as the company crosses breakeven. Price-to-sales is 12.3x and the trailing FCF yield is 1.1%. The forward multiples matter more. The forward P/E is 50.5x, labelled NTM; it matches the $38.90 price over the FY2027 consensus EPS of $0.77, so we treat it as the current-year multiple and use it as the like-for-like reference. On the FY2028 consensus EPS of $0.95, the shares trade at about 41.0x. One caution on basis: the FY2027 consensus EPS is far above the FY2026 diluted EPS of -$0.02 and the thin trailing operating margin set out in the financials, and the page does not say whether the Street's estimates are on a GAAP basis, so the forward and trailing multiples may not compare. Our scenarios therefore all use the consensus earnings basis. With no peer multiples available, we do not call the current-year multiple a premium or a discount to anything; the question is whether it holds as growth slows. The price sits between the 52-week low of $23.38 and the high of $47.47, and no captured source explains the fall from the high.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Anchor: the Street's median target of $53.00. Growth holds near 30% as ARR and large-customer counts keep compounding, consensus earnings rise, and the market pays more for FY2028 earnings a year out than the 50.5x it pays for current-year earnings today. This is the case in which the Street's median view proves right.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Anchor: 45x the FY2028 consensus EPS of $0.95, a year out, a multiple we assume below today's current-year multiple because consensus has revenue growth slowing in FY2027 and the company expects further deceleration (risks section). Samsara delivers the consensus earnings path, and the multiple compresses as growth slows.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Revenue growth slows faster than consensus expects, so consensus-basis EPS stops growing after FY2027 and FY2028 comes in no higher than the FY2027 estimate of $0.77. Anchor: the 52-week low of $23.38, a price the market paid within the past year. On that flat EPS it is a multiple well below both of today's forward multiples, the reset we would expect once the market stops pricing the shares for growth.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
The scenarios weight to a fair value of $40.47, an expected upside of 4.0% against a bear-case downside of 39.9%, for a reward/risk of 0.10×. That derives HOLD: expected upside is below the 10.0% BUY bar and above the -5.0% SELL line, and reward/risk is far below 0.50×.

The Base carries 50% because the latest quarter and the half-year pace in the growth section are consistent with the consensus path. The Bull and Bear carry 25% each because the evidence on each side is of similar strength. For the Bull, every analyst target sits above the price; against it, the Bull needs a higher multiple a year out while growth slows. For the Bear, the company expects slower growth, and the shares traded at the Bear's price within the past year and are well off the 52-week high noted above; against it, multi-year, generally non-cancelable subscriptions limit how fast revenue can fall, and free cash flow is positive.

Sensitivity runs both ways. Holding today's current-year multiple in the Base lifts expected upside above the BUY bar but leaves reward/risk below it, so the label stays HOLD; cutting the Base to today's FY2028 multiple puts it at about today's price, and the label still holds. Moving ten points of weight from Bear to Bull, or from Bull to Bear, also keeps HOLD. Combining the changes is not symmetric: the current-year multiple with ten points moved toward the Bull still derives HOLD, because the deep Bear keeps reward/risk down, while the FY2028 multiple with ten points moved toward the Bear derives SELL. HOLD is the call, and the one combination that crosses a line crosses to SELL.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Samsara reports as a single segment, so FY2026 revenue of $1.6B appears as one consolidated line. Growth within that line comes from new customers and from selling more Applications and Agents to existing customers and expanding them across geographies and divisions, which the MD&A describes as expanding within the existing customer base. The move beyond fleets, discussed in the growth section, is a stated direction that no captured figure yet measures. The business is one platform sold by subscription, so its economics rise or fall with that single subscription base.

moatFactors.name: Switching costs
moatFactors.body: Subscription contracts typically have an initial term of three to five years and are generally non-cancelable and non-refundable, subject to limited exceptions, and the MD&A says the platform and IoT devices are highly interdependent and form a combined performance obligation. Replacing a bundled hardware-and-software layer mid-contract should be costly for a customer, though without a retention or net-expansion figure we cannot measure how strong the effect is.

moatFactors.name: Multi-product adoption
moatFactors.body: The proxy filed June 1, 2026 reports that at the end of FY2026, 96% of customers with over $100,000 in ARR subscribed to 2+ products and 69% of those customers subscribed to 3+ products. Customers using several products are more embedded than single-product users, which supports the land-and-expand model among large accounts.

moatFactors.name: Data asset
moatFactors.body: The same proxy says Samsara processed more than 25 trillion data points in FY2026, which the company says enables its AI models to deliver deeper actionable insights. We have no evidence on whether rivals could build a comparable dataset, so we treat this as a possible advantage rather than an established one.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat narrow. The evidence for it is structural: the contract terms and bundling set out under switching costs, and broad multi-product adoption among large customers. The evidence against it is mostly missing: no retention, net-expansion or competitor figure was captured, and the 10-K lists increased competition among the factors that could slow growth. The move beyond fleets, which the company itself calls uncertain, would test whether the same switching costs hold in new use cases. A wide rating would need retention evidence we do not have; a rating of none would ignore contract terms and adoption figures that point to real switching costs.

points: Annual recurring revenue was $2,124,742 thousand as of August 1, 2026, against $1,640,113 thousand a year earlier, a pace close to the latest quarter's revenue growth and a level above FY2026 revenue. Because revenue is recognized ratably, that base supports further revenue growth if contracts renew, but ARR is not running ahead of revenue, so it does not signal a reacceleration, and the company says ARR is not a forecast.

Customers over $100,000 in ARR rose to 3,605 from 2,771 over the same year, which the MD&A ties to the company's focus on larger customers, its partner ecosystem and the release of more Applications. That count keeps pace with ARR, so large accounts are growing with the base rather than lagging it.

The proxy filed June 1, 2026 reported $1.9 billion in ARR at the end of FY2026, up 30% year over year in constant currency, and 3,194 customers above that ARR threshold, up 29% year over year. Both measures were higher by August, so neither has stalled since fiscal year-end.

Revenue for the six months ended August 1, 2026 rose to $987.3 million from $758.4 million, a half-year pace similar to the latest quarter's. Consensus has FY2027 revenue at $2B, up 26%, and FY2028 revenue at $2.5B; the FY2027 estimate implies a second half slower than the half just reported, so it does not look stretched on the evidence so far.

New use cases: the 10-K says the company has increased its focus on Applications for equipment, sites and frontline workers, but that it is uncertain it will achieve the same penetration and organic growth there as with fleets.

management.leadership: According to the proxy statement filed June 1, 2026, Sanjit Biswas, a co-founder, is Chief Executive Officer and Chair of the Board. Co-founder John Bicket is Executive Vice President and Chief Technology Officer, Dominic Phillips is Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, and Adam Eltoukhy is Executive Vice President and Chief Administrative Officer and Corporate Secretary. Lara Caimi, formerly President of Worldwide Field Operations, stepped down effective March 3, 2025 and left the company on September 5, 2025. Both co-founders voluntarily received a minimal base salary of $50,000 each in FY2026, and the proxy says executive compensation is primarily delivered in the form of equity. The company is founder-led, and pay leans on equity rather than cash, which ties executives to the share price but adds to the equity compensation discussed under capital allocation.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation is reinvestment. Samsara pays no dividend and no buyback figure was captured (cash flow section), and the MD&A says the company expects research and development, sales and marketing, and general and administrative expenses to increase in absolute dollars for the foreseeable future. The 10-K says future operating expenses will include a significant amount of stock-based compensation for RSUs already granted and any equity awards granted in the future, which will impact profitability levels. No stock-based compensation figure was captured, so we cannot size that cost or the dilution it brings. With positive free cash flow and cash and short-term investments on the balance sheet, nothing captured suggests the company needs outside capital. Equity compensation is therefore the capital-allocation item that matters most for outside holders, and the one we can least measure.
management.governance: The proxy filed June 1, 2026 says the Board has determined that eight of its ten directors are independent under NYSE rules: Mr. Andreessen, Mr. Bluedorn, Ms. Bostrom, Mr. Chadwick, Ms. Henry, Ms. Livermore, Mr. Steele and Ms. Wagner. Mr. Biswas holds both the Chief Executive Officer and Chair roles; the excerpt is truncated before any further description of board leadership. One related-party arrangement stands out: the company has a block charter agreement for an aircraft that Mr. Biswas beneficially owns through a limited liability company, operated by a third-party aviation company, and it paid $1,019,318 for business use in FY2026. The company says it pays an amount below market rates for comparable travel and that the agreement may be terminated on 30 days' prior written notice. A majority-independent board is a check, but with the combined Chief Executive Officer and Chair role and the voting structure set out under insider ownership, outside holders rely more on the founders' alignment than on board control.
management.insiderOwnership: As of April 15, 2026, the proxy counts 370,981,108 Class A shares, with one vote each, and 211,728,974 Class B shares, with ten votes each. Mr. Biswas beneficially owned 99,968,305 Class B shares, or 39.6% of total voting power, and Mr. Bicket 95,533,040 Class B shares, or 38.4%; neither holds a majority alone. The 12 directors and executive officers as a group held 90.3% of the Class B shares and 77.5% of total voting power. By contrast, Baillie Gifford & Co., an outside holder in the table, owned 15.5% of the Class A shares but 2.3% of the vote. If insiders vote together, outside Class A holders cannot carry a vote against them, and because each Class B share carries ten votes, insiders' voting power is well above their share of the equity.

idiosyncratic: Slowing growth against a high multiple: the 10-K says Samsara expects its revenue growth rate to continue to decline, including as a result of the maturation of its business. The valuation section shows the expected return depends on the multiple compressing only modestly as that happens; ARR growth falling clearly below revenue growth would be an early sign of a faster slowdown.

Thin operating profit: with the narrow operating margin set out in the financials section, the spending increases described under capital allocation could return the company to operating losses, and the 10-K says it may not achieve or sustain profitability in future periods. A quarter with a negative operating margin would show it happening.

Hardware costs: cost of revenue includes the amortization of connected device costs, so the hardware-price exposure noted in the financials section may reach gross margin across the bundled subscriptions; a further step down in gross margin would show it.
Founder control: the insider voting power set out under management limits outside holders' influence on all matters submitted to a stockholder vote.
risks.systemic: The MD&A says unfavorable economic conditions may negatively affect the growth of the business and its results. It lists inflationary pressure, foreign-currency fluctuations, interest-rate increases, supply-chain and freight disruptions, increased prices for many goods and services, labor shortages, delayed or reduced spending on technology, and new trade and tariff policies. Samsara's customers operate in transportation, construction, logistics, manufacturing and other physical industries, and the 10-K lists macroeconomic factors among the reasons its growth rate could decline. Public-sector customers are often subject to annual budget appropriations cycles, which the company names as an exception to its standard contract terms, and the MD&A says foreign-currency exposure has increased as the company expanded globally. None of these is specific to Samsara, but a stock priced on the current-year multiple discussed under valuation has less room to absorb a macro-driven slowdown than one priced for slower growth.

body: We rate Samsara HOLD with a $36 to $44 target range. The business has turned GAAP-profitable, keeps adding recurring revenue and large customers, and generates free cash flow. But our scenarios weight to a fair value of $40.47, a small expected return against a bear case that returns the shares to their 52-week low, because the Base pays less for FY2028 earnings a year out than the market pays for current-year earnings today. That keeps us one notch below the Street's consensus Buy.

The target range roughly brackets the prices at which these scenarios derive HOLD: BUY derives somewhat below the target low, and SELL from a little below the target high, close to the Base value. Inside that band, the label moves only if new evidence moves the multiple or the weights, as the valuation section's sensitivity shows.
